forces.title: AI fuels growth in advanced and mature node components
forces.description: AI's rapid proliferation is boosting demand for a broad range of advanced and mature-node applications and products beyond leading-edge chips. This includes workload-specific connectivity and data flow components, as well as data center power electronics, which fall under the electronic components and connectors category. This sustained demand provides a positive impetus for the sector, though average selling prices for these components are expected to fall, indicating a focus on volume rather than price appreciation.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: India's defense sensor ecosystem heavily reliant on imports
forces.description: India's defense sensor market, projected to reach $3.5–$4 billion by 2030, currently meets approximately 80% of its demand through imports. This high dependency, particularly in critical fabrication and packaging stages (90-100% import reliance), exposes the country to significant supply, control, and sovereignty risks. This structural vulnerability necessitates aggressive indigenization efforts to ensure national security and resilience in mission-critical defense systems, driving demand for local component production.

forces.title: Government policies accelerate domestic defense sensor manufacturing
forces.description: India's 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' vision and policies like DAP 2020 and Positive Indigenization Lists aim to accelerate indigenous defense manufacturing, directly boosting demand for domestically produced sensors. While current frameworks provide a foundation, sensor-specific initiatives such as a National Sensor Roadmap, PLI scheme, ToT framework, and strategic fab partnerships are emerging as critical enablers to achieve self-reliance and capture domestic value by 2030, driving significant growth opportunities for the sector.

forces.title: Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) Expansion
forces.description: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), originally notified in April 2025, saw its outlay expanded to Rs. 40,000 crore (US$ 4.53 billion) in the Union Budget 2026-27. This scheme is specifically designed to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical electronic components and chips, which currently constitute a large portion of India’s electronics imports. This significant financial outlay and focused policy support act as a strong tailwind for domestic electronic component manufacturing and localization efforts.

forces.title: Major investment boosts domestic PCB and CCL manufacturing capacity
forces.description: Syrma SGS Technology's investment of Rs. 1,800 crore (US$ 210.1 million) to establish India’s largest PCB (Printed Circuit Board) and CCL (Copper Clad Laminate) facility in Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, represents a significant upside driver for the Electronic Components & Connectors sector. This investment directly addresses the need for localized manufacturing of fundamental electronic inputs, supporting India's ambition to build stronger domestic supply chains and reduce import dependency in critical component categories like PCBs.

forces.title: Record electronics import bill driven by component and semiconductor demand
forces.description: India's electronics import bill surged to a record US$ 116.17 billion in FY2025–26, an increase of 17.76% year-on-year. This growth was significantly driven by higher imports of electronic components and semiconductors, alongside finished equipment. This rising import dependence on components represents a key risk for the domestic electronic components and connectors industry, highlighting the challenge of achieving self-sufficiency despite government initiatives and the need for accelerated local manufacturing.

forces.title: Mobile phone scheme fosters domestic component sourcing and design
forces.description: The new Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) enhances its incentive structure by offering additional benefits (up to 1.5%) for sourcing key components and sub-assemblies domestically, beyond a base incentive on eligible sales. A further 3% incentive is available for product design, R&D, and Indian-brand manufacturing. This shift from solely rewarding volume to prioritizing in-country value addition directly benefits the electronic components and connectors sector by driving demand for locally manufactured PCBs, displays, and other sub-assemblies.
forces.source_title: Chips, phones, and the Viksit Bharat playbook

forces.title: 5G and IoT rollouts accelerate electronics product adoption
forces.description: Major technology transitions such as the widespread rollout of 5G networks and the increasing adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) applications are significantly driving the accelerated uptake of electronic products. This surge in demand for sophisticated electronic devices translates directly into a tailwind for the electronic components and connectors sector, as these foundational technologies require a diverse range of advanced and passive components, sensors, and connectivity solutions for their functionality and widespread deployment.

viewpoints.title: Advanced & Mature Nodes See Slower Growth Compared to Leading-Edge Chips
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that while AI fuels strong growth in leading-edge chips and memory, advanced and mature-node applications, which include workload-specific connectivity, data flow components, and data center power electronics (relevant to IN080306), will experience more modest growth through 2030. Sales volume will increase, but average selling prices (ASPs) for this segment are expected to fall, indicating a less robust profitability outlook compared to advanced semiconductors.
viewpoints.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

viewpoints.title: India's Defense Sensor Ecosystem Highly Import-Dependent, Posing Sovereignty Risks
viewpoints.description: Bain highlights that India's defense sensor market, despite rapid growth projections to $3.5–$4 billion by 2030, remains critically reliant on imports, with approximately 80% of demand met externally. This high dependency, particularly in critical fabrication and packaging stages (90-100% import reliance), exposes the country to significant supply, control, and sovereignty risks across mission-critical defense systems, necessitating aggressive indigenization efforts for electronic components like sensors.

viewpoints.title: India Can Achieve Significant Domestic Defense Sensor Value Capture by 2030
viewpoints.description: Bain asserts that India has the potential to capture approximately $1 billion of its domestic defense sensor demand by 2030. This can be achieved through strategic initiatives focused on localizing packaging and module assembly, scaling domestic players, and strengthening the pathways from R&D to commercialization. This indicates a positive outlook for the domestic electronic components sector (specifically sensors), contingent on effective policy execution and targeted investments.

viewpoints.title: National Policy on Electronics to Position India as a Global ESDM Hub
viewpoints.description: The National Policy on Electronics (NPE) 2019 envisions establishing India as a global hub for Electronic System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) by fostering domestic capabilities in core components, including chipsets. This initiative, integrated with "Make in India" and "Digital India," aims to create a globally competitive environment. This reflects strong government support and a positive long-term vision for India's electronic components and connectors sector.

viewpoints.title: Policy Shift Rewards Domestic Value Addition in Mobile Phone Manufacturing
viewpoints.description: India's new Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) shifts its focus from merely incentivizing production volume to rewarding in-country value addition. Companies can earn additional incentives for domestically sourcing key components and sub-assemblies, such as PCBs, displays, and batteries, along with product design and R&D within India. This strategic redirection fosters a positive environment for local electronic component manufacturers by driving demand for deeper domestic integration.
viewpoints.source_title: Chips, phones, and the Viksit Bharat playbook

demand_drivers.description: India’s defense electronics spend is growing at 12%–16% annually, driven by the increasing share of capital outlay within the defense budget and platform modernization programs.
The rising electronics content across various defense platforms is a significant factor driving increased demand for sophisticated sensor systems.
The government's 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' vision and policies are accelerating indigenization, creating sustained demand for domestically manufactured defense sensors and components.

new_opportunities.description: India aims to capture ~$1 billion of domestic defense sensor demand by 2030 by localizing packaging and module assembly, scaling domestic players, and strengthening R&D-to-commercialization pathways.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Domestic Value Capture in Defense Sensors

new_opportunities.description: Prioritizing early localization of sensor module assembly in critical categories like RF sensors presents a key opportunity for domestic manufacturers.

Maturing domestic sensor packaging capabilities, especially for EO/IR and MEMS inertial/pressure sensors, offers significant potential for reducing import reliance and increasing local value addition.

market_sizing.methodology: India's defense sensor market is estimated based on defense electronics spend, rising capital outlay, platform modernization, and increasing electronics content across defense platforms. The forecast to 2030 is driven by the mission criticality of sensor systems and India's accelerating indigenization push. Current market value is $1-1.5 billion, projected to reach $3.5-4 billion.

demand_drivers.description: Robust demand for electronic hardware products and components across diverse sectors, including consumer electronics, IT, telecom, and defense, fuels overall ESDM market expansion.
Government initiatives such as 'Digital India' and 'Make in India', alongside favorable FDI policies, streamline the establishment of manufacturing units and encourage ESDM growth.
The accelerating pace of digitalization across the economy is driving the adoption of electronic systems and components in various applications.

new_opportunities.description: Schemes like ECMS, with significant financial outlays, are attracting investments to localize production of components that currently account for a large share of India’s electronics imports.
The inclusion of board designing and embedded systems within the ESDM definition highlights opportunities in Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) and integrated component solutions.

market_sizing.methodology: The Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) market includes electronic hardware products and components relating to IT, office automation, telecom, consumer electronics, aviation, aerospace, defense, solar photovoltaic, nano electronics, and medical electronics. It also encompasses design activities like product design, chip design, VLSI, board design, and embedded systems. Growth is attributed to strong demand, supportive government policies, and increased digitalization.
